# @alexify/metaschema

> Zero-dependency metadata schema and interface definition language (IDL) for Node.js and
> browsers. Declare data structures and domain models as plain JavaScript objects, validate data
> against them (every error is collected with its path, nothing throws on bad data), and generate
> TypeScript interfaces from a model. A fork of metarhia/metaschema maintained by Alexis
> Technologies.

Key facts:
- Package (npm): `@alexify/metaschema`, installed with `npm install @alexify/metaschema`
- Node.js >= 18 and browsers; CommonJS with ESM named-import interop; hand-written `index.d.ts`
- Zero runtime dependencies, 17.3 KB min+gzip for the core entry (the generators subpath adds
  7.1 KB, the compile subpath 4.0 KB, the model subpath 11.7 KB, the stream subpath 1.0 KB);
  about 10 million checks a second of a flat struct on the closures, about 30 million compiled
- Exports: `Schema`, `Model`, `getKindMetadata`, `SchemaDefinitionError`, `ValidationResult`,
  the constants `KIND`, `KIND_STORED`, `KIND_MEMORY`, `SCOPE`, `STORE`, `ALLOW`, the types
  `Infer`, `InferOutput`, `InferSchema`, `InferEntity`, `CustomTypes`, the locales
  `@alexify/metaschema/locales/en` and `@alexify/metaschema/locales/uk`, the generators
  `@alexify/metaschema/generators`: `toJSONSchema(target, options)`, `toTypeScript(target,
  options)`, `saveTypes(file, target, options)`, `fromJSONSchema(document, options)`,
  `register()` (installs them as methods), the JIT backend `@alexify/metaschema/compile`:
  `compile(target, { jit })` → `{ accelerated, error }`, `register({ jit, onFallback })`,
  `canEval()`, and the model tools `@alexify/metaschema/model`: `fromJSON(snapshot, options)`,
  `diff(prev, next)`, `compatibility(changes)`, `sample(schema, options)`, `merge(a, b,
  options)`, `infer(samples, options)`, `register()` (installs `Model.fromJSON`, `Model.diff`,
  `Model.compatibility`, `Schema.merge`, `Schema.infer`, `schema.sample`), and the record tools `@alexify/metaschema/stream`:
  `checkEach(schema, records, options)`, `parseEach(schema, records, options)` (generators of
  `{ index, record, result }`), `checkEachAsync`/`parseEachAsync(schema, records, options)`
  (async generators, `options.concurrency` records in flight), `transform(schema, options)` (a
  `TransformStream`), `register()` (installs them as methods of `Schema`)
- `checkEach(schema, rows)` checks every record of an iterable and yields `{ index, record,
  result }` in order, lazily; `parseEach` does it with `parse`; `maxInvalid: n` ends the
  iteration after the n-th invalid record; the async pair takes a sync or async iterable and
  keeps `concurrency` records in flight, in order; `transform(schema, { onInvalid, mode, async,
  maxInvalid })` is a `TransformStream` that passes the parsed values of valid records on and
  ends with `ERR_INVALID_RECORD` for an invalid one it was not told to drop
- `model.toJSON()` (what `JSON.stringify(model)` writes) is the model as data, format 1: the
  entities in dependency order with kind, scope, store, allow, parent, unknown, custom, fields
  (each `{ type, required, ...sorted keys }`), indexes and relations, and the types the entities
  use; a function is `{ $function: true }`, a bigint `{ $bigint }`, a Date `{ $date }`, a
  RegExp its source; `fromJSON(snapshot)` restores a model with placeholders for the functions
- `diff(prev, next)` (models or snapshots) lists changes `{ kind: entity | field | index |
  relation | type, op: added | removed | changed | renamed, entity, name, from, to, detail }`,
  a field renamed through `aliases` is `renamed`; `compatibility(changes)` is `full`,
  `backward` (new readers read old data), `forward` (old readers read new data) or `none` by
  the Confluent rules (an optional or defaulted field added or removed is full, a required one
  added is forward and removed backward, `integer` → `number` is backward, a bound tightened is
  forward, enum values added backward)
- A field with `aliases: ['old']` is read from `old` by `check` when the value has nothing
  under the field's key (reported under the key found), and `parse` writes it under the field's
  key; `deprecated: true` is metadata (JSON Schema `deprecated`, dts `@deprecated`, an expected
  removal in `diff`)
- `sample(schema, { seed, locale, references, maxDepth })` is a value `check` accepts, the
  same for a seed, drawn from the definition (lengths, bounds, enums, unions, nested structs,
  collections, references by kind, a pattern from the subset alternatives/groups/classes/
  escapes/quantifiers, a custom type through `metadata.sample`); a field no draw satisfies is
  `ERR_UNSATISFIABLE`
- `fromJSONSchema(document, { name, as, references, unsupported })` reads the subset of JSON
  Schema a validation schema is made of (types, properties/required, enum/const, items and
  tuples, anyOf/oneOf, `$ref` into the definitions, the rules, null, the annotations) into a
  definition or a Schema; a keyword outside it is `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA` with a JSON pointer
- `merge(a, b)` unifies two schemas CUE-style: the constraints of both per field, a conflict is
  `ERR_MERGE_CONFLICT`
- `infer(samples, { as, name, kind, enum, integer, map, maxDepth })` is the reverse of `sample`:
  a definition (or a Schema) every sample passes, from one pass over the values: the kinds of
  every place (a union when several), records fused into one struct with optional keys (absent
  or undefined) and nullable keys (null beside a type), `integer` for whole numbers, an `enum`
  for a string of at most 8 values each seen twice on average, `{ object: { string: T } }` for
  records whose keys are not names or many sparse keys of one kind; no bounds, patterns,
  references or tuples; the definition is checked against every sample before it is returned
  (`ERR_INFER_MISMATCH` is a bug), a sample nested past `maxDepth` is `ERR_INFER_DEPTH`
- `compile(schema)` or `compile(model)` replaces the check with a function generated from the
  schema and built with `new Function` (the same issues, about three times faster on a flat
  struct, six on a nested one) and returns `{ accelerated }`; `register()` does it for every
  schema built afterwards; where code generation from strings is not allowed (CSP, Cloudflare
  Workers, `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings`) the closures stay (`jit: 'auto'`), or
  `jit: true` throws `ERR_NO_EVAL`; the generated source holds no value of the schema, only
  identifiers, numbers and JSON strings (the rest goes through a scope)
- `schema.check(value, options)` returns a `ValidationResult`: `valid`, `issues` (one
  `{ code, path, message, params }` per problem, `path` an array of keys), `errors` (the lines
  with the location), `summary`, `flatten()`, `tree()`; options `root`, `maxErrors`, `maxDepth`
  (embedded records, 128 by default: deeper is a `depth` issue, not a stack overflow),
  `unknown`, `references`, `messages`; a `validate` function may build and return a result
- `schema.parse(value, options)` runs the same check and returns `{ valid, value, issues }`: the
  value of the program with every `default` of a missing key filled in (a function is a
  factory), unknown keys stripped with `unknown: 'strip'`, the `parse` function of every field
  decoding its validated value (parts before the whole: a date string into a `Date`) and
  the schema's own `parse` last; `value` is `undefined` when invalid and the value given when
  nothing applied (the input is never written to). `schema.serialize(value, { check })` is the
  way back through the `serialize` functions, top down. `checkAsync` and `parseAsync` await
  validators, custom `checkType`s and decoders that return promises (settled after the walk, in
  field order); the synchronous calls throw `ERR_ASYNC_VALIDATOR` for a promise
- Every schema is a Standard Schema v1 (`schema['~standard']`, whose `validate` is `parse` with
  the schema's policies, a promise for a schema with async functions; the Standard JSON Schema
  converter `jsonSchema` joins it after `register()` of the generators); `InferSchema<typeof
  schema>` is the TypeScript type of a value it accepts, `InferOutput<typeof schema>` of the
  value `parse` gives
- `toJSONSchema(schema, { target, profile, io, unrepresentable, references, definitions })` and
  `toJSONSchema(model, { root, ... })` render JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (default), draft-07, an
  OpenAPI 3.0 schema object or a MongoDB `$jsonSchema`; `profile: 'strict'` is the dialect of LLM
  structured outputs (root object, every property required, optional as `[T, 'null']`,
  `additionalProperties: false`, no value constraints); a stored reference is an id, a memory
  reference a `$ref`; `validate` functions are not exported
- A broken definition throws `SchemaDefinitionError` (a `TypeError`) with `code`, `schema` and
  `field`, when the schema is built, never during `check`
- Safe to bundle and minify: identity checks use a global symbol brand, not class names
- Field syntax: `'string'`, `'?string'` (optional), `'key?'`, `{ type, ...options }` (`type`
  first), `{ type, nullable: true }`, `{ array: T }`, `{ set: T }`, `{ object: { string: T } }`,
  `{ map: { string: T } }`, `{ enum: [...] }`, `{ union: [...], discriminator? }`, tuples
  `['number', 'number']`, `'json'`, references by capitalized name (`'Company'`,
  `{ many: 'Address' }`: the id of a stored kind, the record of a memory kind)
- Types: `string`, `number`, `integer`, `bigint`, `boolean`, `date`, `null`, `any`/`unknown`,
  `enum`, `array`, `set`, `object`, `map`, `tuple`, `union`, `json`; rules `length`/`pattern`
  for strings, `length` for collections, `min`/`max` for numbers
- Kinds via a capitalized first key: `Entity`, `Registry`, `Dictionary`, `Journal`, `Details`,
  `Relation`, `View` (stored), `Struct`, `Scalar`, `Form`, `Projection` (memory), or any custom
  kind
- `new Model(types, entities, database)` resolves references and orders entities;
  `toTypeScript(model)` renders the interfaces (`{ named: true }` names enums and nested structs,
  a field's `description` is its JSDoc and `deprecated: true` adds `@deprecated`)
- Does not load schemas from files or evaluate source strings; pass schema objects directly
